definitions.gloss: to build up, to construct over time, to establish
definitions.explanation: To create something substantial through sustained effort over time. Often used for abstract accomplishments like careers, reputations, relationships, or fortunes, as well as physical structures.

examples.japanese: {信頼|しんらい}{関係|かんけい}を{築|きず}き{上|あ}げる。
examples.english: To build up a relationship of trust.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{一代|いちだい}で{財産|ざいさん}を{築|きず}き{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: He built up his fortune in a single generation.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}かけて{築|きず}き{上|あ}げてきた{実績|じっせき}が、{今|いま}の{成功|せいこう}につながっている。
examples.english: The track record built up over many years has led to today's success.

notes:
GRAMMAR:
Ichidan compound verb: {築|きず}く (to build) + {上|あ}げる (to raise up). The {上|あ}げる component adds the nuance of completion and accumulated effort.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {信頼|しんらい}を{築|きず}き{上|あ}げる: to build up trust
- {財産|ざいさん}を{築|きず}き{上|あ}げる: to amass a fortune
- {地位|ちい}を{築|きず}き{上|あ}げる: to establish a position
- {実績|じっせき}を{築|きず}き{上|あ}げる: to build up a track record
- {文明|ぶんめい}を{築|きず}き{上|あ}げる: to build a civilization

SIMILAR WORDS:
{築|きず}く on its own also means "to build" but is more neutral. {築|きず}き{上|あ}げる emphasizes the cumulative, effortful process of building something significant from nothing.
